messages:
maya: Quick sync: we need to pick a rollout pattern for the continuous-batcher prototype. I sketched three distinct approaches (sidecar coalescer, node-replace, and split-router) + a short test plan. Thoughts?

devin: Curious about sidecar perf hit. Give short pros/cons.

maya: Sidecar coalescer:
- run a lightweight coalescer as a sidecar on each GPU node, forwards packed requests to new runtime
- pros: zero-touch routing, can toggle per-node, incremental rollout
- cons: extra network hop, memory copies, harder to reason about tail latency

sasha: How do we keep kvcache locality with sidecar? that seems dicey.

maya: Sidecar will carry a "kvcache_affinity" token and preferred shard id in binary meta. We'll attempt local placement by best-effort hint. No strong guarantees.

devin: Node-replace?

maya: Node-replace:
- replace the coalescer binary on a set of nodes with the new runtime (feature-flagged)
- pros: fastest hot path, single codepath, lower overhead
- cons: migration blast radius, requires coordinated rollout and instant rollback plan

jen: Split-router option?

maya: Split-router:
- routing layer decides per-request: legacy vs batched runtime based on size/probe
- pros: fine-grained control, backpressure centralized
- cons: more routing logic, two admission models to reconcile

riley: If we do split-router, admission must remain authoritative in one place. Can we surface expected token cost back to scheduler?

maya: Yes, router sends cost hints to scheduler via the existing admission RPC. We'll keep a single ledger and tag tickets with path id. Reconciliation job required.

sasha: Required metrics: path-latency histograms, kvcache hit by path, batch packing efficiency, fallback/replay counts, per-tenant cost delta.

devin: Testing checklist: unit handshake, kvcache integration with warm/cold scenarios, chaos test (kill sidecar/node mid-batch), 48h perf run with injected slow tails, canary escalation plan.

jen: Security: any reservation or affinity tokens need HMAC with short TTL. Use KMS to sign.

maya: Rolling plan I propose: 1) sidecar PoC in dev cluster 2) small node-replace on isolated pool (perf compare) 3) split-router canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% if stable. Each stage has automatic rollback if fallback > 1% or p99 increases > 20%.

infra-bot: Canary-schedule: planned 2026-06-10T01:00:00Z for pool batch-dev-02 (dry-run)

riley: Cost model stub: sidecar adds ~2-6% CPU; node-replace reduces per-token CPU by ~7-10% in bench. Need more samples.

sasha: One implementation note: prefer compact proto metadata on the wire for internal paths, expand only in traces.

maya: Agreed. I'll draft the design PR with a short proto sketch, rollout plan, and observability owner list. Assign owners: Devin (canary ops), Sasha (kvcache tests), Jen (security/KMS), Riley (cost modelling).

maya: Will open PR tomorrow and paste link here. Ping if you want to pair. :rocket:
